name: How do you know if a gut renovation needs structural engineering?

mainEntity.name: What signs mean a gut renovation in Los Angeles needs an engineer instead of just a contractor?
mainEntity.text: What signs mean a gut renovation in Los Angeles needs an engineer instead of just a contractor?

acceptedAnswer.text: A structural engineer is usually necessary when the renovation affects how the house carries weight. That includes removing load-bearing walls, enlarging openings, changing roof or floor framing, adding heavy finishes or systems, or repairing foundation or framing problems. Older Los Angeles homes often benefit from engineering input even when the scope seems straightforward, because hidden conditions can complicate the project. If there are cracks, sagging floors, prior additions, or a history of settling, engineering review becomes even more important. Homeowners should involve the engineer early so the plans, permit set, and construction details all align. That reduces redesign, avoids field confusion, and helps the project pass inspection more smoothly.
acceptedAnswer.description: A structural engineer is usually needed when the project removes load-bearing walls, changes floor framing, modifies openings, adds loads, or corrects foundation or framing problems. If the house has visible movement, cracking, or plans for major layout changes, engineering review is especially important.
